subsystems.name: Robot units
subsystems.role: small mobile machines that each carry a little material and know how to place it.
parts: wheels, tracks or rotors for movement

subsystems.name: Localisation and sensing
subsystems.role: lets every robot know where it is and where the structure edge currently is, without GPS indoors.
parts: cameras and laser or depth sensors

subsystems.name: Coordination layer
subsystems.role: decides who builds what next using only local rules and neighbour messages, so no central controller is needed.

subsystems.name: Material and deposition
subsystems.role: delivers concrete, mortar or interlocking bricks to the build face.
parts: brick hopper or concrete pump and hose

subsystems.name: Structure and interface design
subsystems.role: shapes the building so that small robots can build it without scaffolding.
parts: build-order rules baked into the design

subsystems.name: Site supervision and safety
subsystems.role: keeps people out of the swarm's working zone and gives a human an overview.

buildSteps.title: Design for swarm assembly
buildSteps.detail: The building is decomposed into units weighing a few kilograms to tens of kilograms, with a build order that never needs temporary supports and never lets one robot block another.

buildSteps.title: Build the robots
buildSteps.detail: Small wheeled or tracked bases are fitted with a manipulator or print head, a battery and a radio; each carries the same coordination software so any unit can be swapped in.

buildSteps.title: Establish a shared coordinate frame
buildSteps.detail: Markers or a surveyed reference grid are set up on site; robots start from known positions and then track each other visually to stay aligned to a few millimetres.

buildSteps.title: Stock and stage material
buildSteps.detail: Bricks, mortar or printing feedstock are placed at depots robots can reach, since each robot carries only enough for a few placements before returning.

buildSteps.title: Build up the structure
buildSteps.detail: Robots claim the next free placement from local information, deposit material, and move on, like termites adding to a mound with no foreman.

buildSteps.title: Verify each other's work
buildSteps.detail: Neighbouring robots scan completed sections and flag or redo a block that is out of tolerance before the layer above is placed.

buildSteps.title: Hand over to human trades
buildSteps.detail: Robots complete the repetitive shell; electricians, plumbers and roofers follow on behind, working to the as-built geometry the swarm has recorded.

buildSteps.title: Scale the swarm
buildSteps.detail: More units and more depots allow bigger structures, with throughput limited by the slowest step, not by the number of robots.

prerequisites.why: swarms must hold millimetre accuracy indoors and among moving machines; marker-based and visual methods work only in controlled settings.
researchers have shown robots building block structures with no central controller, but only for small, simple shapes.
placement accuracy and payload must survive dust, vibration and weather on a real site.

prerequisites.tech: Deposition and adhesion of structural material
prerequisites.why: printed or glued joints must reach the strength of conventional construction reliably.

prerequisites.tech: Battery energy density and wireless mesh networking
prerequisites.why: they set how long a robot can work and how reliably the swarm can talk.

pathway.milestone: laboratory swarms laying foam blocks and flying robots assembling small towers
pathway.unlocks: proof that coordination without a central controller can produce a real structure.

pathway.milestone: drone-based additive manufacturing demonstrated on a tall freeform print
pathway.unlocks: repair and building in places people cannot easily reach, such as bridges, towers and remote sites.

pathway.milestone: supervised swarms on live sites handling repetitive shell work
pathway.unlocks: faster, more predictable construction with fewer workers in hazardous positions.

pathway.milestone: fully autonomous site teams mixing ground and aerial robots
pathway.unlocks: rapid housing and disaster recovery at a speed human crews cannot match.

pathway.milestone: swarms building structures where no human crew can go
pathway.unlocks: habitats and infrastructure in extreme environments, including in space.
